# std.bitset

A dense set of positions of a domain, 64 per word.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Bitset`.

## `struct Bitset<D>`

One bit per position of `D`, in `ceil(K / 64)` words.

Fields: `w: List<U64>`, `n: Int`.

- `fn new() -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; The empty set, every word zero; the same set as `empty()`.
- `fn empty() -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; The empty set, matching `Subset<D>.empty` (a call here: it is O(K / 64)); the same as `new()`.
- `fn full() -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; The full set containing every position of `D`, matching `Subset<D>.full`.
- `fn single(i: D) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; The singleton set `{i}`, matching `Subset<D>.single(i)`.
- `fn from(a: [D]Bool) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K) time, O(K / 64) space; The set of positions where `a` is true.
- `fn of(xs: List<D>) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64 + xs.len) time, O(K / 64) space; Build a bitset from a list or generator of positions `D`.
- `fn contains(self, i: D) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether position `i` is set; `i in b` calls it.
- `fn add(mut self, i: D) -> Bool` — O(1); Set the bit at position `i`; returns `true` if `i` was not already set (matches `Set.add`).
- `fn remove(mut self, i: D) -> Bool` — O(1); Clear the bit at position `i`; returns `true` if `i` was set (matches `Set.remove`).
- `fn toggle(mut self, i: D)` — O(1); Flip the bit at position `i`: set it if clear, clear it if set.
- `fn with(self, i: D) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; A copy of `self` with `i` added; `self` is unchanged.
- `fn without(self, i: D) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; A copy of `self` with `i` removed; `self` is unchanged.
- `fn set(self, i: D, on: Bool) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; A copy of `self` with `i` added if `on` or removed otherwise, matching `Subset<D>.set`.
- `fn complement(self) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; The complement of `self` within `D`, matching `Subset<D>.complement`; bits past the last position stay clear.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — O(K / 64); Remove every position from the set.
- `fn any(self, pred: D -> Bool) -> Bool` — O(K / 64 + visited) words scanned and calls of `pred`; True when some position in this set satisfies `pred`.; traps: never (beyond what `pred` traps on)
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — O(1); The number of positions in the set; the count is kept current by every update.
- `@get fn count(self) -> Int` — O(1); The same number as `len`, under the name C++ gives it.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether the set has no members.
- `fn first(self) -> ?D` — O(K / 64); The smallest position in the set, or `None`.
- `fn find(self, pred: D -> Bool) -> ?D` — O(K / 64 + visited); The smallest position in the set satisfying `pred`, or `None`, as `seq.find`.; traps: never (beyond what `pred` traps on)
- `fn rfind(self, pred: D -> Bool) -> ?D` — O(K / 64 + visited); The largest position in the set satisfying `pred`, or `None`.; traps: never (beyond what `pred` traps on)
- `fn union(mut self, o: Bitset<D>)` — O(K / 64); Replace `self` with `self \| o` in place, with no allocation.
- `fn intersect(mut self, o: Bitset<D>)` — O(K / 64); Replace `self` with `self & o` in place, with no allocation.
- `fn subtract(mut self, o: Bitset<D>)` — O(K / 64); Clear every bit set in `o` from `self` in place: `self - o`.
- `fn symmetric(mut self, o: Bitset<D>)` — O(K / 64); Replace `self` with `self ^ o` in place.
- `fn bitor(self, o: Bitset<D>) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; `a \| b`: a new set of the positions in either set.
- `fn bitand(self, o: Bitset<D>) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; `a & b`: a new set of the positions in both sets.
- `fn bitxor(self, o: Bitset<D>) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space; `a ^ b`: a new set of the positions in exactly one of the sets.
- `fn meets(self, o: Bitset<D>) -> Bool` — O(K / 64), less on an early hit; Do the two sets share a position?
- `fn shifted(self, k: Int) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K / 64) time and space, for any `k`; A new set with every position `k` places up (down for a negative `k`); positions that leave `D` are dropped.
- `fn shift_up(mut self, k: Int)` — O(K / 64); Shift every position `k >= 0` places up in place; bits past `D` drop.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn shift_or(mut self, k: Int)` — O(K / 64); In-place `self \|= self << k` for `k >= 0`, with zero allocation: the knapsack step "every reachable sum, and every reachable sum plus `k`".; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn each(self) -> yields D` — O(K / 64 + len) to walk, O(1) per member amortized; The positions in the set, in increasing order; `for v in b` walks the same sequence.
- `fn next(self, i: D) -> ?D` — O(K / 64); The first position in the set at or after `i`, or `None`.
- `fn prev(self, i: D) -> ?D` — O(K / 64); The last position in the set at or before `i`, or `None` (the mirror of `next`).
- `fn count_below(self, i: D) -> Int` — O(K / 64); The number of positions in the set strictly before `i`.
- `fn subset_sums(weights: List<Int>) -> Bitset<D>` — O(K sqrt(S) / 64) time, where S is the sum of `weights`; O(K / 64) space; All subset sums in `0..D.K` reachable from non-negative `weights`: the position with ordinal `s` is set exactly when some sub-multiset of `weights` sums to `s`.; traps: when a weight is negative
- `fn shift_down(mut self, k: Int)` — O(K / 64); Shift all bits down by `k >= 0` positions in place (`i -> i - k`); bits below `D` drop.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn count_range(self, r: Range<D>) -> Int` — O(r.len / 64 + 1); Count set bits in `r` (accepts cut ranges via decision 124).
- `fn set_range(mut self, r: Range<D>, on: Bool = true)` — O(r.len / 64 + 1); Set (or, with `on: false`, clear) every bit in `r` in place.
- `fn flip_range(mut self, r: Range<D>)` — O(r.len / 64 + 1); Flip every bit in `r` in place.
- `fn nth(self, k: Int) -> ?D` — O(K / 64); The `k`-th set position (0-based, in increasing order), or `None` if `k >= len`.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn each_rev(self) -> yields D` — O(K / 64 + len) to walk; The set positions in descending order.

## `struct DynBitset`

Runtime-sized 64-bit word bitset over `0..cap` when the width is computed dynamically without a domain.

- `fn new(cap: Int) -> DynBitset` — O(cap / 64) time and space; Create an all-zero `DynBitset` of width `cap`: bits `0..cap`.; traps: when `cap < 0`
- `fn full(cap: Int) -> DynBitset` — O(cap / 64) time and space; Create an all-one `DynBitset` of width `cap`; bits at or above `cap` stay clear.; traps: when `cap < 0`
- `@get fn cap(self) -> Int` — O(1); The bit capacity: valid indices are `0..cap`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — O(1); The number of set bits, kept current by every update.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether no bits are set, kept current by every update.
- `fn contains(self, i: Int) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether bit `i` is set.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn set(mut self, i: Int, on: Bool = true)` — O(1); Set bit `i` to `on` in place (W8 `IndexSet` backing `b[i] = on`).; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn add(mut self, i: Int) -> Bool` — O(1); Set bit `i` to 1; returns `true` if bit `i` was previously 0 (matches `Bitset.add`).; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn remove(mut self, i: Int) -> Bool` — O(1); Clear bit `i` to 0; returns `true` if bit `i` was previously 1 (matches `Bitset.remove`).; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn toggle(mut self, i: Int)` — O(1); Flip bit `i`.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn clear(mut self)` — O(cap / 64); Clear all bits; the capacity is unchanged.
- `fn resize(mut self, new_cap: Int)` — O(new_cap / 64) time and space; Resize to `new_cap` bits, zero-filling any new high bits.; traps: when `new_cap < 0`
- `fn first(self) -> ?Int` — O(cap / 64); The smallest set bit index, or `None` if empty.
- `fn last(self) -> ?Int` — O(cap / 64); The largest set bit index, or `None` if empty.
- `fn next(self, i: Int) -> ?Int` — O(cap / 64); The smallest set bit `>= i`, or `None`.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..=cap`
- `fn prev(self, i: Int) -> ?Int` — O(cap / 64); The largest set bit `<= i`, or `None`; `i` itself counts, as in `Bitset.prev`.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..cap`
- `fn count_below(self, i: Int) -> Int` — O(cap / 64); The number of set bits strictly below `i`.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..=cap`
- `fn count_range(self, r: Range<Int>) -> Int` — O(r.len / 64 + 1); The number of set bits in `r`.; traps: when `r` is non-empty and reaches outside `0..cap`
- `fn nth(self, k: Int) -> ?Int` — O(cap / 64); The `k`-th set bit index (0-based, in increasing order), or `None` if `k >= len`.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn union(mut self, other: DynBitset)` — O(cap / 64); In-place bitwise OR (`self \|= other`).; traps: when `other.cap != self.cap`
- `fn intersect(mut self, other: DynBitset)` — O(cap / 64); In-place bitwise AND (`self &= other`).; traps: when `other.cap != self.cap`
- `fn subtract(mut self, other: DynBitset)` — O(cap / 64); In-place set difference (`self &= ~other`).; traps: when `other.cap != self.cap`
- `fn symmetric(mut self, other: DynBitset)` — O(cap / 64); In-place bitwise XOR (`self ^= other`).; traps: when `other.cap != self.cap`
- `fn meets(self, other: DynBitset) -> Bool` — O(cap / 64), less on an early hit; Whether `self` and `other` share a set bit; stops at the first shared word.; traps: when `other.cap != self.cap`
- `fn shift_up(mut self, k: Int)` — O(cap / 64); Shift all bits up by `k >= 0` in place (`i -> i + k`); bits reaching `cap` or beyond drop.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn shift_down(mut self, k: Int)` — O(cap / 64); Shift all bits down by `k >= 0` in place (`i -> i - k`); bits falling below 0 drop.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn shift_or(mut self, k: Int)` — O(cap / 64); In-place `self \|= (self << k)` for `k >= 0`, with zero allocation; bits reaching `cap` drop.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn each(self) -> yields Int` — O(cap / 64 + len) to walk; The set bit indices in ascending order; `for i in d` walks the same sequence.
- `fn each_rev(self) -> yields Int` — O(cap / 64 + len) to walk; The set bit indices in descending order.
- `fn subset_sums(cap: Int, weights: List<Int>) -> DynBitset` — O(cap sqrt(S) / 64) time, where S is the sum of `weights`; O(cap / 64) space; All subset sums in `0..cap` reachable from `weights`: bit `s` is set exactly when some sub-multiset of `weights` sums to `s`.; traps: when `cap < 0` or a weight is negative

## `struct XorTrie`

O(bits) per op.

- `fn new(bits: Int = 60) -> XorTrie` — O(1); Create an empty `XorTrie` over `bits`-bit non-negative integers (default 60): values in `0..2^bits`.; traps: when `bits` is not in `1..=62`
- `fn reserve(mut self, nodes: Int)` — O(nodes) time and space; Reserve pool capacity for at least `nodes` trie nodes, so later adds do not reallocate; the contents are unchanged.; traps: when `nodes < 0`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — O(1); The total number of stored integers, with multiplicity.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — O(1); True when the trie holds no integers.
- `fn add(mut self, x: Int)` — O(bits) time, up to `bits` new nodes; Insert one copy of `x`.; traps: when `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn remove(mut self, x: Int) -> Bool` — O(bits); Remove one copy of `x`; returns `false` if absent, leaving the trie unchanged.
- `fn contains(self, x: Int) -> Bool` — O(bits); Whether `x` is present at least once.
- `fn count(self, x: Int) -> Int` — O(bits); The multiplicity of `x` currently stored; zero when absent.
- `fn xor_all(mut self, mask: Int)` — O(1); Apply a lazy global XOR mask: every stored `y` becomes `y ^ mask`.; traps: when `mask` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn max_xor(self, x: Int) -> ?Int` — O(bits); The maximum value of `x ^ y` over stored `y`, or `None` if empty.; traps: when `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn min_xor(self, x: Int) -> ?Int` — O(bits); The minimum value of `x ^ y` over stored `y`, or `None` if empty.; traps: when `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn count_xor_less(self, x: Int, limit: Int) -> Int` — O(bits); The number of stored `y` (with multiplicity) with `(x ^ y) < limit`.; traps: when `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn kth_xor(self, x: Int, k: Int) -> ?Int` — O(bits); The `k`-th smallest value of `x ^ y` over stored `y` (0-based, with multiplicity), or `None` if `k >= len`.; traps: when `k < 0` or `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn mex_xor(self, x: Int = 0) -> Int` — O(bits); The smallest non-negative integer not present under XOR mask `x` (mex of `{y ^ x}`); `2^bits` when every value is present.; traps: when `x` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn clear(mut self)` — O(1); Remove all elements and the global mask, keeping `bits` and the reserved pool.

## Example

```cp
domain B = 0..8
var bs = Bitset<B>()
bs.add(B(1))
bs.add(B(4))
print(bs.count)
// output: 2
```
